reviews.title: Loved this one!
reviews.body: I love this one! I've done a few of these books now since I saw "The Killer Isn't Alice", and i think this may be the best one so far. It's not just crossing off names, there are other things you have to look for, like a place, or cause of death. It still took several days, so it wasn't finished too fast, but didnt take a month either. Totally recommend this!!

reviews.title: Great concept, but data professionals beware
reviews.body: This is well put together and I can see why people enjoy it, but if your day job involves data analysis, databases, metadata, or writing business rules, this may feel much more like work than recreation. The “puzzles” are largely applying successive filtering criteria to thousands of rows of data. My immediate reaction was not “Ooh, a mystery!” but “I could put this in a database and solve it with a query.”I was expecting more individual logic puzzles and deductive reasoning; instead, much of the challenge appears to be manually executing filters. That's probably very satisfying if this kind of data manipulation is novel to you. If you do it professionally, however, you may find yourself wondering why you're spending your free time manually doing something you'd automate at work.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on 29 August 2026

reviews.title: Not what expected. Disappointed
reviews.body: I misread and assumed files meant multiple cases not files for one case. It didn’t work for the what I planned for a group. Okay for just me but limited since it’s only 1 case. Very disappointed.
